fix.summary: Three sustained package defects are established on current HEAD. Repair nullable Git-object validation, make the accepted receipt carry exact accepted-leg identity and enforce complete terminal coverage, and replace the underspecified one-line axis question with a deterministic package-owned axis output adapter. No owner choice or new Plan is required; preserve the exact canonical Skill snapshot, common readable material, verbatim reports, and the irreversible accepted batch.

classes.name: Nullable pinned-ref and Git object-ID contract
classes.owner: `src/package-contracts/reviewer-output.ts` owns validation of the target identity projected into `RuntimeReviewerReceiptV2`; `src/reviewer-git-snapshot.ts` remains the source type/parser for ref entries.
classes.boundary: Validate every Git object ID against `target.objectFormat`: exactly 40 lowercase hexadecimal characters for `sha1` and 64 for `sha256`. Apply that law to `targetHead`, each ref `objectId`, and each non-null `peeledCommitId`. A ref entry must have exactly `{objectId, peeledCommitId}`; `objectId` is always a valid ID, while `peeledCommitId` is either `null` or a valid same-format ID. `null` is lawful for refs whose object does not peel to a commit and must not be converted to an empty string or rejected. Preserve exact closed-key validation.
classes.disposition: Direct Fixer repair. Current `src/package-contracts/reviewer-output.ts:78` requires `peeledCommitId` to be a string, contradicting `ReviewerRefEntry` and `parseReviewerRefSnapshot`. Add receipt regressions for lawful null, lawful same-format IDs, wrong width, non-hex/uppercase IDs, and invalid nullability.

classes.name: Authenticated accepted-leg coverage in Runtime Reviewer receipts
classes.owner: The accepted dispatch/ledger owns expected leg identity and terminality; `src/reviewer-settlement.ts` projects it into the runtime receipt; `src/package-contracts/reviewer-output.ts` owns standalone receipt validation and Recorder consumption.
classes.boundary: A receipt for an accepted batch must carry a closed accepted-batch projection, not only an opaque `batchIdentity`: the accepted dispatch identity plus the exact canonical expected legs in order (`standards` alone, or `standards` then `spec`), including each compiled prompt identity. Settlement must derive this projection from `record.accepted.legs`, never from submitted intent or observed outcome keys. Receipt validation must require outcome keys to equal the expected axes exactly and each outcome prompt identity to equal its accepted leg prompt. Every expected leg is terminal. Reports must equal the successful-axis set exactly: one valid verbatim report for every successful outcome and none for failed outcomes. `completed` requires every expected outcome successful; accepted `refused` still requires every expected outcome terminal and preserves reports for all successful legs. Pre-acceptance `refused` has no accepted-batch identity, outcomes, or reports. Extra, missing, duplicate, reordered, or noncanonical expected axes are invalid. Cardinality is derived from the authenticated expected-leg list rather than a separately drifting count.
classes.disposition: Direct Fixer repair. Current receipt validation accepts a nonempty successful subset as completed and zero/partial outcomes after accepted refusal, despite the ledger enforcing exact settlement. Add one- and two-leg completed/refused matrices, missing/extra-axis cases, prompt mismatch, success/report mismatch, and pre-acceptance refusal regressions through package validation and native-session recording.

classes.name: Axis-specific package output adapter and semantic audit alignment
classes.owner: The package-owned Reviewer construction recipe/compiler owns child transport and output mechanics; the unchanged external canonical Skill snapshot owns semantic Standards/Spec briefs and baseline; the post-settlement Reviewer compliance auditor owns semantic enforcement of the compiled axis contract.
classes.boundary: For each accepted leg, deterministically compile an axis-specific method adapter into the exact prompt identity (and, where appropriate, the child system/output envelope). It must state that the full canonical Skill snapshot remains semantic input, but its dual-agent orchestration, dual-axis aggregation, and dual-section presentation template are superseded for this already-isolated leg. The Standards leg answers only the canonical Standards question and baseline burden; the Spec leg answers only the canonical Spec question. Each emits one substantive report for its assigned axis under an axis-typed/fixed output envelope, with no second-axis assessment, count, conclusion, or section. Both children retain the same exact canonical Skill file and common material population and may read or cite any material. The runtime preserves returned report bytes verbatim: it must not parse headings, sanitize prose, split sections, rewrite output, or create replacement legs. Update the semantic auditor's supplied method contract so it treats the package adapter as controlling presentation/output mechanics while the Skill controls substantive semantics; it rejects answering the other question, but never rejects merely for cross-axis material access or citation.
classes.disposition: Direct Fixer repair under the existing recipe/audit owners. Review-033 and Review-034 independently show both fixed-question children following the canonical Skill's dual-axis presentation, satisfying the prior judgment's explicit reopen condition. The present prompts at `src/reviewer-dispatch.ts:365` provide only a one-line question while exposing the complete dual-axis Skill, so this is now reproducible construction ambiguity rather than invocation-only behavior. Prove deterministic axis-distinct prompt/envelope identities, unchanged Skill/common-bundle bytes, verbatim report preservation, no prose parser, and audit acceptance/revision against the lawful single-axis contract.

details.note: The raw Review-034 child sessions corroborate the summary: both reports contain `## Standards` and `## Spec`, while their compiled prompts assign distinct questions. Existing owner law already resolves the design: canonical semantic content remains external input, while the package recipe controls mechanical assembly and output transport. Therefore escalation is unwarranted. This judgment does not authorize source/material allowlists, global Skill edits or forks, report sanitization, driver aggregation, replacement legs, or weakening truthful refused receipts.
